Gniewoszów (Regów Dolny) Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Regów Nowy, Poland

Demolished. Granica - later absorbed into Gniewoszów after World War II - had a small Jewish community by the mid-18th century; a 1745 by-law issued by the town's owner recorded the cemetery's location, likely close to its founding. By 1921, 651 Jews lived in Granica, nearly two-thirds of the population; most were murdered at Treblinka in 1942. The cemetery itself was dismantled during the war, its stones and walls repurposed for construction, and later used as pasture and a limestone depot. Poland formally closed it by ministerial order in 1964, with documentation noting a final burial in 1945. In 2016, the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage and the ESJF fenced the site with German government funding, though a 2018 survey found the fence damaged and the gate missing.
